sources.entry: AI Canvas Tauri - Free, lightweight, source-available AI canvas for storyboarding, image and video creation, editing, and asset management with ComfyUI workflows. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A local-first desktop AI canvas (Tauri 2 + React) for storyboarding, image/video generation, AI short-drama production and asset management, with ComfyUI and MCP integration.
summary.what_it_does: Organizes text, image, video, audio, frame-animation, Markdown, storyboard, 360° panorama and sketch-note content as connectable nodes on a canvas. Connects to cloud and custom AI models plus ComfyUI servers and general workflow APIs, and can run ComfyUI workflows. Includes a resource library for project and global assets (characters, scenes, props, weapons) with prompts, tags and reference images. Supports frame-animation editing with GIF/PNG/atlas export, a built-in video editor, and a chat assistant that can query or edit the canvas. Projects can be split into episodes, each with its own canvas while sharing the character library. The README also describes optional S3-compatible project sync, MCP control over stdio or Streamable HTTP (off by default), and a plugin system for JavaScript and Python plugins.
use_cases: organizing character, scene and prop assets
how_to_run: npm run dev  (web frontend only; plugins and desktop features unavailable)
npm run tauri dev  (full desktop app, requires Rust stable toolchain)
npm run tauri build  (build desktop installer)
notable: Node-based canvas mixing media types, with ComfyUI workflow import and execution
Episode/season structure where each episode has its own canvas but shares the character library and memory
Chat-based agent that can query/edit the canvas and generate media, plus MCP control over local stdio or Streamable HTTP
JavaScript and trusted Python user plugin system
Local-first storage with a separate credential store for API keys
caveats: Source-available, not OSI open source: commercial resale, white-label and competing commercial use are prohibited; the README says the code will switch to MIT only after 10,000 GitHub stars.
Many features (plugins, file system, credential storage, standalone windows, 3D director stage, local models) require the Tauri desktop environment; the online demo is limited.
Blender-based advanced 3D editing is optional and supports only specific Blender versions on Windows x86_64 or macOS; Windows builds need Visual Studio Build Tools 2022.
